scope: V1 documentation, sanitized source/assets/prepared-demo records, and all local Git history
source_identity_note: Full app/server/build checks ran before history rewriting; rewriting changed only historical commit references in the roadmap at the tip. This verification record and final handoff documentation are added afterward.
private_identifier_scope: Git author/committer names and email addresses
local process IDs in verification records

git_cleanup.commit_timestamps: original UTC calendar date at midnight
git_cleanup.private_recovery_bundle: outside app repository; verified; contains unsanitized originals; do not share

image_text_scan.limitation: OCR is a screening aid; it cannot prove absence of every visible identifier. Public course/instructor names and synthetic app identities remain.

limitations: This is an identifier/metadata cleanup and regression check, not a complete security audit, independent educational review or production acceptance.
Legal credits, source URLs, functional identifiers, synthetic fixtures and model attribution are retained. Some positive production-gate fixtures deliberately use production-like fictional addresses.
Public sources were not downloaded again; their original upstream hashes are retained separately from sanitized distributables.
No new interactive browser, native-device, live identity-provider, paid-model or deployment acceptance was performed.
Tests are bounded samples, not a long-duration memory-stability guarantee.
OS-managed provenance attributes remain on working files; Git and the clean source archive do not include those attributes or filesystem ownership.
Private recovery bundles, previous copies, installed dependencies, browser/editor history and GitHub account/audit metadata are outside the distributed source cleanup.
The local repository has no remote and has not been uploaded by this cleanup.
